answer: Randomized admission lottery. Each period, a verifiable randomness beacon (VRF) draws a slot count from identities committed in advance. A hidden commitment is only scored if its hash falls below the draw threshold, so attackers cannot precompute which identities will land in the haven of admitted slots. The ripple effect: surplus identities are excluded, and their work cost is lost. Each attempt costs the full registration deposit plus lost compute, making mass timber of fake accounts uneconomic.
